⭐ RESUMEN GENERAL — Versión combinada para aprobar (45 min)
⭐ VERSIÓN COMBINADA · TU RESUMEN + ESQUEMA DEL COMPAÑERO
Resumen General del Examen · 45 min
✅ Imprescindible🎯 También puede caer🔴 Rojo / ✗ = trampa🟢 Verde / ✓ = correcto🔵 Azul = ejemplo🟨 Subrayado = palabra clave🔥 T40 y T41 = los que más salen
Cómo estudiarlo (45 min): 10 bloques, cada tema con su ficha. 1ª vuelta → solo tablas y bloques ✅ IMPRESCINDIBLE (~30 min). 2ª vuelta → los 🎯 y las cajas de colores (~15 min). Termina SIEMPRE con las 20 trampas de oro del final. Al final de cada bloque tienes una caja ➕ También lo preguntan: es lo que sale en las preguntas de la app y no estaba en el resumen. Debajo de cada bloque tienes botones ✏️ Test para hacer su test al momento. Los T40 y T41 son mezclas donde caen muchísimas preguntas: repaso doble.

1T1 — Present Simple⭐⭐⭐
✅ IMPRESCINDIBLE
▸ +S/ES en he/she/it: works, watches, goes, studies · have → has
▸ Negativa/pregunta: do/does + infinitivo: Does she work? ✗ Does she works
▸ Adverbios de frecuencia: antes del verbo, después de BE: She always arrives late / She is always late
Ortografía 3ª personaEjemplo
regla general +splays, works
-s, -sh, -ch, -x, -z, -o → -eswatches, fixes, goes, does
consonante + y → -iescry → cries
vocal + y → -splay → plays
🎯 TAMBIÉN PUEDE CAER
▸ Usos: hábitos, verdades generales, horarios oficiales (The train leaves at 6)
▸ Con who sujeto: Who works here? (sin auxiliar)
2T2 — Pasado Simple⭐⭐⭐
✅ IMPRESCINDIBLE
▸ Regulares -ED; irregulares de memoria (T19)
▸ Negativa/pregunta: did + infinitivo: Did you go? ✗ Did you went
▸ Marcadores: yesterday, last week, ago (siempre al final), in 1999, when…?
Ortografía -EDEjemplo
general +edworked
acaba en -e → +dlive → lived
1 sílaba C-V-C → doblastop → stopped, plan → planned
consonante + y → -iedstudy → studied
vocal + y → +edplay → played
🎯 TAMBIÉN PUEDE CAER
▸ Pronunciación: /t/ worked · /d/ played · /ɪd/ wanted, needed
▸ used to para hábitos pasados (ver T40)
6T6 — Presente Continuo⭐⭐
✅ IMPRESCINDIBLE
▸ am/is/are + -ing: acción ahora, situación temporal, citas ya fijadas (I'm meeting him tomorrow)
▸ Verbos estáticos NO van en continuo: ✗ I am knowing → I know (T27)
Ortografía -INGEjemplo
general +ingtalking
-e muda se valive → living, make → making
1 sílaba C-V-C → doblaswim → swimming, run → running
-ie → -yinglie → lying, die → dying
🎯 TAMBIÉN PUEDE CAER
▸ always + continuo = queja: He is always losing his keys
▸ Tendencias: Prices are rising · marcadores: now, at the moment, currently, these days
7T7 — Past Continuous⭐⭐⭐
✅ IMPRESCINDIBLE
▸ was/were + -ing: acción en curso en un momento del pasado
▸ WHILE + continuo, WHEN + simple: I was sleeping when the phone rang
▸ Dos acciones simultáneas: While I was cooking, he was reading
🎯 TAMBIÉN PUEDE CAER
▸ When I arrived, she was cooking (ya cocinaba) ≠ When I arrived, she cooked (cocinó después)
▸ Estáticos tampoco en continuo
14T14 — Presente Perfecto⭐⭐⭐
✅ IMPRESCINDIBLE
▸ have/has + participio: experiencia sin momento, resultado presente, acción que sigue
▸ NUNCA con tiempo terminado: yesterday, last week, in 2010, ago → Past Simple
▸ Marcadores: ever, never, just, already, yet, so far, this week, today, since, for
🎯 TAMBIÉN PUEDE CAER
▸ have been to (fue y volvió) ≠ have gone to (se ha ido y está allí)
▸ It's the first time I have… · the best film I have ever seen
▸ Tiempo no acabado: this morning, this year
15T15 — For, Since, Ago, Just, Still, Already, Yet⭐⭐⭐
PalabraSignificadoPosición / usoEjemplo
FORdurante (duración)+ periodofor 3 years
SINCEdesde (inicio)+ punto de iniciosince 2019, since Monday
DURINGdurante+ nombre (evento)during the holidays
AGOhaceal final · Past Simpletwo days ago
JUSTacabar deentre auxiliar y participioI have just eaten
ALREADYyaentre aux. y part. · al final de pregunta = sorpresaShe has already left
YETtodavía (neg.) / ya (preg.)SIEMPRE al finalHas he arrived yet?
STILLtodavía (sigue)antes del verbo · en negativa antes de todoHe still hasn't come
🎯 TAMBIÉN PUEDE CAER
▸ It's two years since I saw her = I haven't seen her for two years
16T16 — Present Perfect Continuous⭐⭐
✅ IMPRESCINDIBLE
▸ have/has been + -ing: duración hasta ahora: I have been waiting for two hours
▸ Explica un resultado visible: You're wet! — I've been running
▸ Estáticos NO: I have known him for years ✗ been knowing
🎯 TAMBIÉN PUEDE CAER
▸ Simple = resultado/cantidad (I've read 3 books) ≠ continuo = duración/proceso (I've been reading all day)
17T17 — Past Perfect⭐⭐⭐
✅ IMPRESCINDIBLE
▸ had + participio: la acción MÁS ANTIGUA de dos pasadas: When I arrived, the train had left
▸ Con before, after, by the time, already, never…before
🎯 TAMBIÉN PUEDE CAER
▸ Reported speech: present perfect / past simple → past perfect
▸ 3er condicional (If I had known…) y wish + had + part.
▸ Inversión: Hardly had he left when… · No sooner had I arrived than…
18T18 — Past Perfect Continuous⭐
✅ IMPRESCINDIBLE
▸ had been + -ing: duración antes de otro momento pasado / causa de un resultado pasado: His eyes were red; he had been crying
🎯 TAMBIÉN PUEDE CAER
▸ Simple = terminado · continuo = duración
19T19 — Verbos Irregulares⭐⭐⭐
✅ IMPRESCINDIBLE
▸ Pasado = participio: bring-brought, buy-bought, catch-caught, teach-taught, think-thought, feel-felt, keep-kept, leave-left, lose-lost, meet-met, pay-paid, say-said, sell-sold, send-sent, spend-spent, tell-told, find-found, hold-held, win-won, make-made, hear-heard, sit-sat, stand-stood
▸ Tres formas distintas: be-was/were-been · begin-began-begun · break-broke-broken · choose-chose-chosen · do-did-done · draw-drew-drawn · drink-drank-drunk · drive-drove-driven · eat-ate-eaten · fall-fell-fallen · fly-flew-flown · forget-forgot-forgotten · give-gave-given · go-went-gone · grow-grew-grown · know-knew-known · ride-rode-ridden · see-saw-seen · speak-spoke-spoken · steal-stole-stolen · swim-swam-swum · take-took-taken · throw-threw-thrown · wake-woke-woken · wear-wore-worn · write-wrote-written
🎯 TAMBIÉN PUEDE CAER
▸ Iguales en las 3: put, cut, hit, let, set, shut, hurt, cost, read (/red/)
▸ a–u–u: ring-rang-rung, sing-sang-sung, run-ran-run, come-came-come
25T25 — Futuro Simple y Futuro Perfecto⭐⭐⭐
FormaCuándoEjemplo
WILLdecisión espontánea, promesa, ofrecimiento, predicción SIN pruebasI think it will rain · I'll help you
BE GOING TOplan previo, predicción CON evidenciaLook at those clouds! It's going to rain
PRESENT CONTINUOUScita/arreglo fijado (fecha, hora)I'm seeing the doctor at 5
PRESENT SIMPLEhorarios oficiales, transportesThe plane leaves at 9
WILL HAVE + part.acabado antes de un momento futuroBy 2030 I will have retired
✅ IMPRESCINDIBLE
▸ Tras when, if, as soon as, until, before, after, unless → PRESENTE: I'll call you when I arrive ✗ when I will arrive
🎯 TAMBIÉN PUEDE CAER
▸ Shall I / Shall we…? (ofrecimientos) · be about to = a punto de
26T26 — Futuro Continuo y Perfecto Continuo⭐⭐
✅ IMPRESCINDIBLE
▸ will be + -ing: en curso en el futuro: This time tomorrow I will be flying
▸ will have been + -ing: duración hasta un futuro: By June I will have been working here for 5 years
🎯 TAMBIÉN PUEDE CAER
▸ at 8 tomorrow → continuo · by 8 → perfecto
▸ Pregunta cortés: Will you be using the car tonight?
27T27 — Verbos Dinámicos y Estáticos⭐⭐
✅ IMPRESCINDIBLE
▸ Estáticos (NO continuo): like, love, hate, want, need, prefer, know, understand, believe, remember, mean, seem, belong, own, cost, contain + sentidos
▸ Dinámicos (acciones): run, work, eat, write → sí continuo
🎯 TAMBIÉN PUEDE CAER
▸ Doble sentido: I have a car / I'm having lunch · I think so / I'm thinking about it · I see / I'm seeing the doctor · taste, smell, weigh, look
▸ She is silly (es) ≠ She is being silly (se está portando así)
➕También lo preguntan · Tiempos verbales🔎
🔎 SALE EN LAS PREGUNTAS DE LA APP
Irregulares que también salen
InfinitivoPasadoParticipio
arisearosearisen
bindboundbound
fleefledfled
forbidforbadeforbidden
freezefrozefrozen
hidehidhidden
lie (yacer)laylain
lightlitlit
meanmeantmeant
shakeshookshaken
shed · spread · hit= igual= igual
swearsworesworn
treadtrodtrodden
withdrawwithdrewwithdrawn
overthrowoverthrewoverthrown
▸ Trampas: found → founded (fundar) ≠ find-found-found · lie → lied (mentir, regular) ≠ lie-lay-lain (yacer)
Concordancia sujeto–verbo
▸ A number of + plural → verbo plural: A number of employees are unhappy · The number of → singular: The number of applicants increases
▸ Singular: asignaturas en -ics (Physics is), cantidades como unidad (Ten euros is not enough · Ten miles is a long way), none of the evidence is, each of / neither of / everybody + singular
▸ Plural: The police are · Both Tom and Ben were · staff / jury / committee: singular (grupo) o plural (miembros)
Usos que faltaban
▸ Presente continuo para cambios y tendencias: The situation is getting worse · Prices are rising · y situaciones temporales: They are building a house this month
▸ Más estáticos (sin -ing): appear, seem, consist of, contain, make sense, suggest (= indicar: The evidence suggests…), weigh (= pesar: It weighs 5 kilos)
▸ Present perfect con: It's the third time (that) the printer has broken · so far, recently, lately, over the last years · has yet to + inf = todavía no ha: The board has yet to decide
▸ Past perfect tras found / discovered / realised / admitted that: They found that the funds had been stolen · con as if: She felt as if she had been running for days · By 1990 the population had doubled
▸ never used to = didn't use to · would + inf solo para acciones repetidas del pasado (We would train every day), nunca para estados
▸ NEED con sentido pasivo: The report needs checking = needs to be checked ✗ needs being checked
📦 Bloque 2 · Nombre y determinantes⏱ 6 min
3T3 — El Artículo⭐⭐⭐
✅ IMPRESCINDIBLE
▸ A / AN por el SONIDO, no por la letra: a book, a university, a European car, a UN report · an hour, an honest man, an FBI agent
▸ A/AN: contable singular, primera mención, profesiones (She is a nurse) ✗ a information
▸ THE: ya mencionado o único (the sun, the planets), superlativos y ordinales (the first prize), fechas y décadas (the 1st of December, the 90s), the internet, the radio, the newspaper, ríos/mares/cordilleras, países plurales o con Republic/Kingdom (the USA, the UK, the Netherlands), the + adjetivo = grupo (the poor, the rich)
▸ SIN THE: plurales e incontables en sentido general (He loves babies, Money isn't everything), países y ciudades (Spain, Madrid), días/meses/años, idiomas, deportes, comidas, con posesivo (her job), watch TV
🔤 SIGLA vs ACRÓNIMO
Sigla (se deletrea) → THE: the FBI, the CIA, the UN, the UK, the USA
Acrónimo (se lee como palabra) → sin THE: NASA, NATO, AIDS, UNESCO
🏫 school · hospital · prison · church · university · bed
Va por su función → sin artículo: He is in prison (está preso) · go to bed / to school
Va de visita o al edificio → THE: He went to the prison to see his uncle
🎯 TAMBIÉN PUEDE CAER
▸ Cargo sin nombre → the President; con nombre → President Lincoln
▸ Expresiones sin artículo: go by train/bus, at home, at work, at night
▸ once a week, twice a day · play the piano (instrumento) / play football (deporte)
4T4 — El Plural de los Sustantivos⭐⭐⭐
Termina enReglaEjemplosExcepciones
general+sbook → books—
-s, -ss, -ch, -sh, -x, -z+esbus → buses, match → matches, box → boxes—
vocal + y+sboy → boys, day → days—
consonante + y-iesbaby → babies, city → cities—
-o+eshero → heroes, potato → potatoes, tomato → tomatoes+s: photos, pianos, radios, videos, zoos, kangaroos, casinos
-f / -fe-vesknife → knives, wife → wives, leaf → leaves+s: roofs, giraffes, chiefs, beliefs
✅ IMPRESCINDIBLE
▸ Irregulares: man → men, woman → women, child → children, person → people, foot → feet, tooth → teeth, goose → geese, mouse → mice · crisis → crises, analysis → analyses, axis → axes, criterion → criteria, phenomenon → phenomena
▸ Igual en singular y plural: sheep, deer, fish, cod, salmon, series, species
▸ Siempre plural (se cuentan con a pair of): scissors, trousers, jeans, glasses, pyjamas, shorts, tights, clothes · people, police → verbo plural
▸ Solo los contables tienen plural · los adjetivos NUNCA: two tall men · sustantivo adjetivado en singular: three mountain bikes, a ten-year-old boy ✗ ten-years-old
🎯 TAMBIÉN PUEDE CAER
▸ news, maths, physics, economics → verbo singular: The news is good
8T8 — Genitivo Sajón y Posesión⭐⭐⭐
✅ IMPRESCINDIBLE
▸ 's con personas, animales, países/ciudades, organizaciones, indefinidos y expresiones de tiempo: Spain's capital, the company's profits, somebody's bag, today's newspaper, a week's holiday
▸ Cosas → OF: the door of the house, the end of the film · organizaciones: las dos (the government's decision / the decision of the government)
▸ ✗ the Jane's pen → ✓ Jane's pen (sin THE delante del poseedor con nombre propio)
PoseedorSe añadeEjemplo
singular'sthe officer's car
singular acabado en -s's o solo 'James's / James' sister
plural en -ssolo 'my brothers' flat, the officers' cars
plural irregular'sthe children's toys, the women's room
indefinido + else's en elseeveryone else's boyfriend
👥 ¿De los dos o de cada uno?
Ann and Michael's flat → 's solo al final = de los dos (un piso)
Ann's and Michael's flats → 's en cada uno = cada uno el suyo
🎯 TAMBIÉN PUEDE CAER
▸ Doble genitivo: Michael's sister's wedding
▸ Se omite casa/tienda: I'm going to Sandra's, at the baker's, at the doctor's
▸ Doble posesivo: a friend of mine, a brother of Maria's
▸ Sustantivo + sustantivo (el 1º hace de adjetivo y va en singular): a mountain bike, a coffee cup
▸ Con verbos: have, own, belong to (That car belongs to me)

▸ Recíprocos: each other (2 personas) · one another (más de 2)
▸ ONE / ONES evita repetir: the red one, the small ones · impersonal: One must be polite, oneself

▸ Cambian de significado: paper / a paper (periódico), glass / glasses, hair / a hair, time / times

➕También lo preguntan · Nombre y determinantes🔎
🔎 SALE EN LAS PREGUNTAS DE LA APP
Artículos
▸ Sin THE: conceptos abstractos en general: Life is short · Nature · Honesty is the best policy · Crime · Justice · Society
▸ Con THE: the majority of, The Hague, the Isle of Wight, the Sahara, the Amazon, the Alps, the First World War, the United Nations, the Supreme Court, the Earth, the Moon
▸ Cargo tras elect / appoint sin artículo: He was elected President of the company · in hospital (como paciente)
Plurales especiales
TipoEjemplos
Compuestos: plural en la palabra principalbrothers-in-law, passers-by, commanders-in-chief, attorneys general · pero bus stops
Latín / griegothesis → theses, analysis → analyses, crisis → crises, criterion → criteria, phenomenon → phenomena, curriculum → curricula, stratum → strata, addendum → addenda
Igualesheadquarters, series, species, sheep, deer, fish · data (is o are)
Genitivo y pronombres
▸ Genitivo de tiempo: five years' experience, next year's budget, tonight's show, today's newspaper · compuesto: my brother-in-law's house · familia: the Smiths' car · someone else's
▸ Peter and I are… (sujeto) · to Peter and me (objeto) · formal: It was he who called
▸ Everybody → their · Each of the officers has his or her / their own locker
▸ Reflexivos fijos: enjoy yourself, make yourself at home, help yourself, by myself, The evidence speaks for itself, The company prides itself on…
▸ Neither… nor / Either… or: el verbo va con el sujeto más cercano: Neither Peter nor his colleagues are aware
▸ would rather + otra persona + PASADO: I'd rather you finished it today · misma persona + inf: I'd rather stay
Cuantificadores formales y partitivos
IncontableContable plural
a great deal of, a large amount ofa large number of, a number of
considerable, insufficient, littlenumerous, several, few
not muchnot many
▸ Most of the officers ✗ almost of the officers
▸ a cup of tea · a glass of water · a slice of cake · a loaf of bread · a bar of chocolate · a pair of jeans · a piece of advice / news / paper / furniture
🎨 Bloque 3 · Adjetivos y adverbios⏱ 4 min
5T5 — Los Adjetivos⭐⭐⭐
✅ IMPRESCINDIBLE
▸ Invariables: nunca plural (two tall men)
▸ Orden OSASCOMP: Opinion · Size · Age · Shape · Colour · Origin · Material · Purpose → a beautiful small old round red Spanish wooden table
-ED-ING
cómo me siento (emoción)lo que provoca (característica)
I am bored / interested / tiredThe film is boring / interesting / tiring
🎯 TAMBIÉN PUEDE CAER
▸ Acaban en -LY pero son adjetivos: friendly, lovely, lonely, silly, elderly, costly
▸ Solo tras verbo: asleep, alone, alive, afraid, awake, aware · solo delante: main, only, former
▸ Linking verbs + adjetivo (no adverbio): She looks happy, It tastes good
▸ fun (divertido) ≠ funny (gracioso)
20T20 — Los Adverbios⭐⭐⭐
AdjetivoAdverbio
general+ly: quick → quickly
-y-ily: happy → happily
-le-ly: sensible → sensibly, gentle → gently
-ic-ally: fantastic → fantastically
irregularesgood → well, true → truly, nice → nicely, fast → fast, hard → hard

✅ IMPRESCINDIBLE
▸ hard (duro) ≠ hardly (apenas) · late ≠ lately (últimamente) · near/nearly · high/highly
▸ Frecuencia: antes del verbo principal, detrás de BE, entre auxiliar y verbo: I have never been
▸ Modo tras el verbo/objeto: He opened the door carefully ✗ opened carefully the door
▸ EVER = alguna vez: preguntas, superlativos (the best I have ever seen), tras palabra negativa (Nobody ever told me)
🎯 TAMBIÉN PUEDE CAER
▸ Orden: modo → lugar → tiempo
▸ Grado: very, quite · too + adj (exceso) · adj + enough

⚖️ LIKE vs AS
AS = función o profesión real (He works as a doctor = es médico) · causa (As it's late, we'll go) · as…as, such as, as usual, as you know, the same as
LIKE = parecido (He works like a slave = no lo es) · look/sound/smell/taste/feel like + nombre (It looks like a burger) pero look + adjetivo (You look tired) ✗ look like tired

Ortografía del comparativo

▸ Inversión: So dangerous was the situation that… · Only after the trial did we learn… · Scarcely had he begun when… · On no account ✗ In no account
▸ Formar adjetivos: poison → poisonous · able → unable · honest → dishonest · stress → stressful

🚨 LAS 20 TRAMPAS DE ORO
Léelas justo antes de cada test. Si te sabes estas 20, tienes la mayoría de preguntas trampa controladas.
1. MUSTN'T = prohibido
→ DON'T HAVE TO / NEEDN'T = no hace falta
2. AGO → Past Simple
→ FOR / SINCE → Present Perfect
3. Tras if / when / unless / as soon as
→ presente, NUNCA will
4. did / does / do +
→ infinitivo (✗ did went)
5. Despite / In spite of + nombre/-ing
→ Although + sujeto + verbo · ✗ despite of
6. SAY (to sb) / TELL sb
→ ✗ said me · ✗ told to me
7. little / few = poco (−)
→ a little / a few = algo (+)
8. THAT nunca en non-defining
→ con comas → who / which
9. ITS = su
→ IT'S = it is
10. A / AN por el SONIDO
→ an hour, a university · the FBI pero NASA
11. Frecuencia antes del verbo
→ detrás de BE
12. Reported: un tiempo atrás
→ tomorrow → the next day · pregunta en orden afirmativo
13. 2º condicional: were + would
→ 3º: had + part. / would have + part.
14. I am → aren't I?
→ Let's → shall we? · never → tag afirmativo
15. used to + inf (solía)
→ be / get used to + -ING
16. SO + adj · SUCH a + adj + nombre
→ TOO + adj · adj + ENOUGH
17. each / every / either / neither
→ verbo singular · both → plural
18. stop / remember / forget / try + to ≠ + -ing
→ cambian de significado
19. have something done
→ make / let sb + inf sin to · get sb TO do
20. Pasiva = BE en el tiempo + participio
→ let → be allowed to · It is said that / He is said to
✅ Rutina recomendada: fin de semana → Resumen completo (45 min) + simulacro. Entre semana → 1 bloque al día (5 min) + test de esos temas + las 20 trampas. Lo que falles en los tests, márcalo aquí y repásalo primero.
T1 — Present Simple
1Forma afirmativa

Sujeto + verbo (+S/ES en 3ª persona). I work · She works · He watches TV. Se añade -ES tras -s,-sh,-ch,-x,-o (watch→watches, go→goes).

2Forma negativa e interrogativa

Con el auxiliar DO/DOES + not. I don't work · She doesn't work. Interrogativa: Do you work? · Does she work? — el verbo principal vuelve a su forma base, sin -s.

3Uso

Hechos y verdades generales (Water boils at 100°C), rutinas y hábitos (I get up at 7), horarios fijos (The train leaves at 9) y estados/sentimientos (I know, She loves).

4Marcadores temporales

always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never, every day/week, on Mondays. Estos adverbios de frecuencia van ANTES del verbo principal pero DESPUÉS de BE: She always arrives late · She is always late.

5Trampa de examen

3ª persona singular con verbos acabados en consonante+Y: cambia a -IES. study→studies, carry→carries. Pero si acaba en vocal+Y: solo +S (play→plays).

T2 — Pasado Simple
1Verbos regulares

Se añade -ED a la forma base: work→worked, play→played. Si acaba en -E, solo +D (like→liked). Consonante+Y → -IED (study→studied). Consonante-vocal-consonante en verbo de una sílaba duplica la consonante final (stop→stopped).

2Verbos irregulares

Tienen una forma propia de pasado que hay que memorizar: go→went, see→saw, have→had, buy→bought. Es la misma para todas las personas (no llevan -S).

3Negativa e interrogativa

Con el auxiliar DID + not, y el verbo principal SIEMPRE vuelve a su forma base (infinitivo sin to), incluso si es irregular: I didn't go (no 'didn't went') · Did she go?

4Uso

Acciones terminadas en un momento concreto y específico del pasado, ya mencionado o implícito. I visited Paris in 2019 · She called me yesterday.

5Marcadores temporales

yesterday, last night/week/year, ago (two days ago), in 2010, when I was young. Si no hay un momento concreto del pasado, normalmente se usa Present Perfect en su lugar.

T3 — El Artículo
1A / AN — indeterminado

Se usa con sustantivos contables en singular, cuando el oyente no sabe exactamente cuál. A + sonido consonántico (a university, /j/), AN + sonido vocálico (an hour, la H es muda; an FBI agent, /ef/). La regla es del SONIDO, no de la letra.

2THE — determinado

Se usa cuando ambos hablantes saben de qué se habla: algo ya mencionado (I saw a dog. The dog was black), único en el mundo (the sun, the moon), superlativos (the best) y con instrumentos musicales (play the guitar).

3Artículo CERO (sin artículo)

No se usa artículo con sustantivos plurales o incontables en sentido general (Dogs are loyal, I like music), con nombres propios, comidas, idiomas, deportes, y con 'go to bed/school/work/church' en su sentido habitual.

4Trampas típicas

Con países que llevan 'Republic/Kingdom/States' → THE: the United States, the UK. Continentes, la mayoría de países y ciudades → sin artículo: Spain, Europe. 'Hospital/prison/school' sin THE = para su función; con THE = el edificio como lugar físico.

T4 — El Plural de los Sustantivos
1Regla general

Se añade -S: book→books, car→cars. Tras -s,-ss,-sh,-ch,-x,-z se añade -ES: bus→buses, box→boxes, watch→watches.

2Terminados en -Y

Consonante+Y → cambia a -IES: city→cities, baby→babies. Vocal+Y → solo +S: boy→boys, day→days.

3Terminados en -F / -FE

Cambian a -VES: knife→knives, wife→wives, leaf→leaves. Excepciones que solo añaden -S: roof→roofs, chief→chiefs.

4Plurales irregulares

man→men, woman→women, child→children, foot→feet, tooth→teeth, mouse→mice, person→people. No siguen ninguna regla, hay que memorizarlos.

5Invariables y sustantivos SIEMPRE plurales

sheep, fish, deer no cambian en plural (one sheep, two sheep). Trousers, glasses, scissors, jeans son siempre plurales y llevan verbo en plural: My trousers ARE dirty (nunca 'a trouser').

T5 — Los Adjetivos
1Posición e invariabilidad

En inglés, los adjetivos van SIEMPRE antes del sustantivo (a big house, nunca 'a house big') y NUNCA cambian de forma: no llevan -S en plural ni distinguen género. Tall boys, tall girls.

2Orden de adjetivos múltiples (OSASCOMP)

Opinion, Size, Age, Shape, Colour, Origin, Material, Purpose + sustantivo. Ej.: a beautiful (opinion) small (size) old (age) round (shape) red (colour) Italian (origin) wooden (material) dining (purpose) table.

3Adjetivos terminados en -ED / -ING

-ED describe cómo se SIENTE una persona (I am bored), -ING describe cómo ES algo o alguien / qué provoca (The film is boring). 'I am boring' significaría que yo aburro a los demás, no que yo esté aburrido.

4Adjetivos que no llevan -LY (aunque parezcan adverbios)

friendly, lonely, lovely, silly, ugly, elderly son ADJETIVOS a pesar de terminar en -ly. No existe 'friendlily'.

5Función atributiva vs predicativa

Atributiva: delante del sustantivo (The big ball broke a window). Predicativa: detrás de un verbo copulativo como TO BE (The ball is big).

6Adjetivos que solo van delante del sustantivo

Los que acompañan a "first/next/last" + número: the first long word, the last three big t-shirts. Sin esa estructura, sí pueden ir en predicado: The film was very long.

7Adjetivos que solo van detrás del verbo (linking verbs)

Con verbos copulativos (be, become, feel, seem, look, taste, smell, sound, go, get, turn) algunos adjetivos solo pueden ir detrás: I feel good. Si no van con estos verbos, pueden ir delante: Good job.

8Adjetivos con prefijo A- (solo tras el verbo)

asleep, awake, alive, afraid, alone... nunca van delante del sustantivo: They were alive (correcto) pero no "the alive people". I was asleep.

9FUN vs FUNNY

FUN = diversión (sustantivo, a veces adjetivo): We had fun. FUNNY = gracioso/que da risa: The film was funny. No se usa "funny" para decir que algo es agradable o divertido sin ser cómico.

10Adjetivos -ED que son también Past Participle

Ojo: no todo lo que acaba en -ED es adjetivo, puede ser Past Simple/Participle del verbo: I was worried (adjetivo) vs You worried me! (verbo, Past Simple). Casos con dos versiones: close (cercano/cerrar) y closed (cerrado).

T6 — Presente Continuo
1Forma

Sujeto + BE (am/is/are) + verbo-ING. I am working · She is working · They are working. Negativa: BE + not (She isn't working). Interrogativa: BE + sujeto (Is she working?).

2Reglas de ortografía del -ING

Verbo acabado en -E muda: se quita la E (make→making). Consonante-vocal-consonante en sílaba tónica: se dobla la consonante (run→running, sit→sitting). Acabado en -IE: cambia a -Y (lie→lying).

3Uso 1: acción en curso ahora mismo

Look! It's raining. · She is studying right now. Se usa con 'now, at the moment, right now, Look!, Listen!'.

4Uso 2: planes futuros ya organizados

I'm meeting my friends tomorrow. · We're flying to Rome on Friday. Indica una cita/plan concreto, no solo una intención.

5Uso 3: situación temporal / tendencia cambiante

He's working in Paris this month (no para siempre) · The climate is changing. Contraste con Present Simple, que expresa permanencia/rutina.

6Verbos que NO se usan en continuo

Verbos de estado (know, like, love, want, believe, understand, need, own) no suelen llevar -ING porque describen estados, no acciones: I know the answer (no 'I am knowing').

T7 — Past Continuo
1Forma

Sujeto + WAS/WERE + verbo-ING. I was working · They were working. Negativa: She wasn't working. Interrogativa: Were you working?

2Uso 1: acción en curso en un momento concreto del pasado

At 8pm yesterday, I was having dinner. Se centra en el proceso, no en si terminó o no.

3Uso 2: acción interrumpida por otra (WHEN / WHILE)

La acción larga en Past Continuous es interrumpida por una acción corta en Past Simple: I was watching TV when the phone rang. WHILE suele introducir la acción larga; WHEN, la acción corta.

4Uso 3: dos acciones simultáneas en el pasado

While she was cooking, he was setting the table. Dos procesos paralelos, ambos en Past Continuous.

5Contraste con Past Simple

Past Simple = acción completa y puntual (The phone rang). Past Continuous = acción en desarrollo, sin foco en su final (I was watching TV). Es la diferencia entre 'telón de fondo' (continuo) y 'evento' (simple).

T8 — Genitivo Sajón
1Forma básica ('S)

Se usa con personas, animales y a veces países/organizaciones para expresar posesión: poseedor + 'S + cosa poseída. Peter's car (el coche de Peter). El orden es inverso al español.

2Plurales regulares (solo apóstrofe)

Si el poseedor ya es plural y termina en -S, solo se añade el apóstrofe, sin otra S: the students' books (los libros de los estudiantes), my parents' house.

3Nombres propios terminados en -S

Se puede añadir 'S completo (más formal/común en el examen) o solo apóstrofe: James's car o James' car. Ambas formas se aceptan.

4Genitivo doble y posesión compartida

a friend of mine (uno de mis amigos). Si dos personas poseen algo JUNTAS, el 'S va solo en el último nombre: Tom and Jerry's flat (el piso que comparten). Si es de cada uno por separado: Tom's and Jerry's cars.

5OF-genitive (posesión con objetos/cosas)

Con cosas inanimadas se prefiere OF en vez de 'S: the roof of the house (no 'the house's roof'), the title of the book.

6Países y ciudades

También se usa 'S cuando el poseedor es un país, ciudad u organización: Italy's architecture is impressive (la arquitectura de Italia es impresionante).

7Omitir el sustantivo ya mencionado

Si el sustantivo poseído ya se ha nombrado antes, se puede omitir y dejar solo el 'S: Whose jacket is this? It's my sister's. (ya sabemos que hablamos de 'jacket'). Peter's car is better than Paul's.

8Pronombres indefinidos (some-/every-/no-/any-)

Con "one" y "body" referidos a personas se usa genitivo: This isn't anybody's business. · Is this someone's seat? Si el pronombre lleva "else", el 'S se pone en "else": Everyone else's boyfriend was here.

9Doble genitivo (dos posesiones seguidas)

Cuando hay dos relaciones de posesión encadenadas, se pueden usar dos genitivos seguidos: We didn't go to Michael's sister's wedding (la boda de la hermana de Michael): una posesión entre Michael y su hermana, y otra entre la hermana y la boda.

10Casa o tienda omitidos

Cuando lo poseído es una casa o una tienda, se puede omitir porque se sobreentiende: I'm going to Sandra's (a casa de Sandra) · Did you buy anything at the butcher's? (en la carnicería).

11OF + pronombre/adjetivo posesivo (con personas)

También se puede indicar posesión de personas con OF + pronombre posesivo: A friend of mine has started to work there. (un amigo mío). Equivale a usar el adjetivo posesivo: My friend has started to work there.

12Sustantivo como adjetivo (sin posesión real)

Un sustantivo puede funcionar como adjetivo de otro sin que haya posesión: mountain bike, love story. Truco: si al poner la frase en plural el "adjetivo" no cambia, es que funciona como adjetivo (church roofs); si añade -S, es un genitivo con OF (the roofs of the churches).

13Error típico: "the" con nombre propio

Con un poseedor que es nombre propio NUNCA se usa "the" delante: John's pen is blue (no "The John's pen"). Pero si el sustantivo ya lleva "the" de por sí, se mantiene: The President's suit was very elegant.

T9 — There Be
THERE BE = HAY / HABÍA / HABRÁ… Expresa que algo existe en un lugar. Siempre lleva un sustantivo detrás y el verbo concuerda con ese sustantivo.
✔ Afirmativa✘ Negativa? Pregunta↩ Resp. corta
🕐 Tiempos verbales
1Present SimpleHay
There is → singular o incontable · There are → plural
✔ Afirmativa
There is / are + sustantivo
There is a dog on the street. (Hay un perro en la calle)
There are three children playing. (Hay tres niños jugando)
There is some cake if you want. (Hay algo de tarta (incontable))
✘ Negativa
There isn't / aren't + sustantivo
There isn't a dog on the street. (No hay un perro)
There aren't three children playing.
There isn't any cake. (No hay nada de tarta)
? Pregunta
Is / Are there + sustantivo ?
Is there a dog on the street? (¿Hay un perro…?)
Are there three children playing?
Is there any cake?
↩ Resp. cortas
Yes, there is / are. · No, there isn't / aren't.
Is there some cake? Yes, there is.
Are there two boys? No, there aren't.
2Past SimpleHabía
There was → singular o incontable · There were → plural
✔ Afirmativa
There was / were + sustantivo
There was a big balloon in the sky. (Había un globo enorme)
There were a lot of animals at the zoo. (Había muchos animales)
There was coffee in her house. (Había café)
✘ Negativa
There wasn't / weren't + sustantivo
There wasn't a balloon in the sky.
There weren't a lot of animals.
There wasn't coffee in her house.
? Pregunta
Was / Were there + sustantivo ?
Was there a balloon in the sky?
Were there a lot of animals?
Was there coffee in her house?
↩ Resp. cortas
Yes, there was / were. · No, there wasn't / weren't.
Was there a blue car? Yes, there was.
Were there two old men? No, there weren't.
3Present PerfectHa habido
There has been → singular o incontable · There have been → plural
✔ Afirmativa
There has / have been + sustantivo
There has been an accident. (Ha habido un accidente)
There have been some errors. (Ha habido varios errores)
There has been peace around here. (Ha habido paz)
✘ Negativa
There hasn't / haven't been + sustantivo
There hasn't been an accident.
There haven't been errors.
There hasn't been peace around here.
? Pregunta
Has / Have there been + sustantivo ?
Has there been an accident?
Have there been any errors?
↩ Resp. cortas
Yes, there has / have. · No, there hasn't / haven't.
Has there been a girl following you? Yes, there has.
Have there been pencils for all? No, there haven't.
4Past PerfectHabía habido
Una sola forma: There had been (todos los sustantivos)
✔ Afirmativa
There had been + sustantivo
There had been improvements in security. (Había habido mejoras)
There had been a plan, but no one followed it.
There had been hate between both countries.
✘ Negativa
There hadn't been + sustantivo
There hadn't been improvements in security.
There hadn't been a plan.
? Pregunta
Had there been + sustantivo ?
Had there been improvements in security?
Had there been a plan?
↩ Resp. cortas
Yes, there had. · No, there hadn't.
Had there been enough money? No, there hadn't.
Had there been political differences? Yes, there had.
5Future SimpleHabrá
Una sola forma: There will be
✔ Afirmativa
There will be + sustantivo
There will be a meeting tomorrow at 5. (Habrá una reunión)
There will be some cookies in the kitchen.
There will be orange juice for everyone.
✘ Negativa
There won't be + sustantivo
There won't be a meeting tomorrow at 5.
There won't be cookies in the kitchen.
? Pregunta
Will there be + sustantivo ?
Will there be a meeting tomorrow?
Will there be orange juice for everyone?
↩ Resp. cortas
Yes, there will (be). · No, there won't (be).
El «be» final es opcional
Will there be soup for dinner? Yes, there will.
Will there be a computer? No, there won't be.
6Be going toVa a haber
Se conjuga como «to be»: There is going to be (singular/incontable) · There are going to be (plural)
✔ Afirmativa
There is / are going to be + sustantivo
There is going to be a surprise. (Va a haber una sorpresa)
There is going to be snow everywhere.
There are going to be two famous singers.
✘ Negativa
There isn't / aren't going to be + sustantivo
There isn't going to be a surprise.
There aren't going to be two famous singers.
? Pregunta
Is / Are there going to be + sustantivo ?
Is there going to be a surprise?
Are there going to be two famous singers?
↩ Resp. cortas
Yes, there is / are going to (be). · No, there isn't / aren't going to (be).
El «be» final es opcional
Is there going to be enough chocolate? Yes, there is going to.
Are there going to be problems? No, there aren't going to be.
7Future PerfectHabrá habido
Una sola forma: There will have been
✔ Afirmativa
There will have been + sustantivo
There will have been cuts before we improve. (Habrá habido recortes antes de que mejoremos)
There will have been love until he goes away.
There will have been a partial examination before.
✘ Negativa
There won't have been + sustantivo
There won't have been cuts before we improve.
There won't have been a partial exam.
? Pregunta
Will there have been + sustantivo ?
Will there have been cuts before we improve?
Will there have been a partial exam?
↩ Resp. cortas
Yes, there will. / Yes, there will have been. · No, there won't. / No, there won't have been.
La 1ª opción (corta) es la MÁS COMÚN
Will there have been cuts before we improve? Yes, there will.
Will there have been music before the cocktails? No, there won't have been.
8Conditional SimpleHabría
Una sola forma: There would be
✔ Afirmativa
There would be + sustantivo
There would be tea for your guests. (Habría té para tus invitados)
There would be two police cars watching everything.
There would be a journalist available.
✘ Negativa
There wouldn't be + sustantivo · Would there be …?
Negativa y pregunta siguen la regla general del condicional
There wouldn't be tea for your guests.
Would there be a journalist available?
9Conditional PerfectHabría habido
Una sola forma: There would have been
✔ Afirmativa
There would have been + sustantivo
There would have been problems everywhere. (Habría habido problemas por todas partes)
There would have been contaminated water.
There would have been a person in charge.
✘ Negativa
There wouldn't have been + sustantivo
There wouldn't have been problems everywhere.
There wouldn't have been water.
? Pregunta
Would there have been + sustantivo ?
Would there have been problems everywhere?
Would there have been water?
↩ Resp. cortas
Yes, there would. / Yes, there would have been. · No, there wouldn't. / No, there wouldn't have been.
La 1ª opción (corta) es la MÁS COMÚN
Would there have been a clear majority? Yes, there would.
Would there have been enough money to do it? No, there wouldn't have been.
⚙️ There + verbos modales
10There can bePuede haber
There can be — todos los sustantivos
✔ Afirmativa
There can be an earthquake soon. (Puede haber un terremoto pronto)
There can be peace if we start talking. (Puede haber paz si hablamos)
✘ Negativa
There can't be an earthquake soon.
There can't be two buses available.
? Pregunta
Can there be an earthquake soon?
Can there be two buses available?
↩ Resp. cortas
Yes, there can. / Yes, there can be. · No, there can't. / No, there can't be.
La 1ª opción (corta) es la MÁS COMÚN
Can there be two winners? Yes, there can.
Can there be another train tomorrow? No, there can't.
11There could bePodría / Pudo haber
There could be — todos los sustantivos
✔ Afirmativa
There could be too many people at the concert. (Podría haber demasiada gente)
There could be food for everyone. (Pudo haber comida para todos)
✘ Negativa
There couldn't be food for everyone. (No pudo haber comida)
There couldn't be a prize for you.
? Pregunta
Could there be too many people at the concert?
Could there be a prize for you?
↩ Resp. cortas
Yes, there could. / Yes, there could be. · No, there couldn't. / No, there couldn't be.
La 1ª opción (corta) es la MÁS COMÚN
Could there be enough power for all of us? Yes, there could be.
Could there be another reason? No, there couldn't.
12There may bePuede / Podría haber
There may be — todos los sustantivos
✔ Afirmativa
There may be a better solution for this. (Podría haber una solución mejor)
There may be journalists outside.
There may be mud everywhere.
✘ Negativa
«May not» NO se contrae
There may not be a better solution for this.
There may not be mud everywhere.
? Pregunta
May there be a better solution for this?
May there be journalists outside?
13There might bePodría haber
There might be — todos los sustantivos
✔ Afirmativa
There might be a hurricane this season. (Podría haber un huracán)
There might be demonstrations tomorrow.
There might be some food for us to eat.
✘ Negativa
«Mightn't» es rarísimo: mejor «might not»
There might not be a hurricane this season.
There might not be demonstrations tomorrow.
? Pregunta
Might there be a hurricane?
Might there be demonstrations tomorrow?
↩ Resp. cortas
Yes, there might. / Yes, there might be. · No, there might not. / No, there might not be.
La 1ª opción (corta) es la MÁS COMÚN
Might there be any famous people? Yes, there might be.
Might there be an improvement? No, there might not.
14There should beDebería haber
There should be — todos los sustantivos
✔ Afirmativa
There should be agents looking for them. (Debería haber agentes buscándoles)
There should be an adult in the class.
There should be clean water for all of us.
✘ Negativa
There shouldn't be agents looking for them.
There shouldn't be clean water for all of us.
? Pregunta
Should there be agents looking for them?
Should there be clean water?
↩ Resp. cortas
Yes, there should. / Yes, there should be. · No, there shouldn't. / No, there shouldn't be.
La 1ª opción (corta) es la MÁS COMÚN
Should there be a digital blackboard? Yes, there should be.
Should there be a warning? No, there shouldn't.
15There must beDebe haber
There must be — todos los sustantivos
✔ Afirmativa
There must be a mistake in these results. (Debe haber un error)
There must be water everywhere.
There must be higher traffic fines.
✘ Negativa
There mustn't be secrets between us. (No debe haber secretos)
There mustn't be violence on tv.
? Pregunta
Must there be secrets between us?
Must there be violence on tv?
↩ Resp. cortas
Yes, there must. / Yes, there must be. · No, there mustn't. / No, there mustn't be.
La 1ª opción (corta) es la MÁS COMÚN
Must there be a reason for his behaviour? Yes, there must.
Must there be consequences? No, there mustn't be.
16There ought to beDebería haber
There ought to be — todos los sustantivos
✔ Afirmativa
There ought to be something to help him remember. (Debería haber algo…)
There ought to be a law against that.
There ought to be more people supporting her.
✘ Negativa
En la pregunta, «to» va después de «there»: Ought there to be…?
There ought not to be a law against that.
There ought not to be more people supporting her.
? Pregunta
Ought there to be a law against that?
Ought there to be more people supporting her?
↩ Resp. cortas
Yes, there ought to. / Yes, there ought to be. · No, there ought not to. / No, there ought not to be.
La 1ª opción (corta) es la MÁS COMÚN
Ought there to be free wi-fi everywhere? Yes, there ought to be.
Ought there to be an extra exam? No, there ought not to.
17There needn't beNo debería haber
There needn't be — SOLO frases negativas
✘ Negativa
There needn't be + sustantivo
There needn't be a reason for this. (No tiene por qué haber una razón)
There needn't be people outside. (No es necesario que haya gente fuera)
⏪ There + modal perfecto (pasado)
18There must have beenDebe haber habido
There must have been — todos los sustantivos
✔ Afirmativa
There must have been something she didn't like. (Debe haber habido algo que no le gustó)
There must have been an error.
There must have been witnesses of the accident.
✘ Negativa
There mustn't have been an error.
There mustn't have been witnesses of the accident.
? Pregunta
Must there have been an error?
Must there have been witnesses of the accident?
19There may / might have beenPuede / Podría haber habido
There may have been / There might have been
✔ Afirmativa
There might have been more tension between both countries.
There may have been another murderer.
✘ Negativa
«May not» no se contrae. «Mightn't» es poco común.
There might not have been enough oxygen for all the astronauts.
There may not have been another murderer.
? Pregunta
May there have been another murderer?
Might there have been enough oxygen?
↩ Resp. cortas
Yes, there might / may. / Yes, there might / may have been. · No, there may / might not. / No, there may / might not have been.
La 1ª opción (corta) es la MÁS COMÚN
May there have been an alternative? Yes, there may.
Might there have been an agreement between the two parts? No, there might not have been.
20There could have beenPodría haber habido
There could have been — todos los sustantivos
✔ Afirmativa
There could have been more opportunities for all students.
There could have been a hole in the plane.
✘ Negativa
There couldn't have been a hole in the plane.
There couldn't have been more opportunities for all students.
? Pregunta
Could there have been a hole in the plane?
Could there have been more opportunities for all students?
↩ Resp. cortas
Yes, there could. / Yes, there could have been. · No, there couldn't. / No, there couldn't have been.
La 1ª opción (corta) es la MÁS COMÚN
Could there have been other options? Yes, there could have been.
Could there have been a happier way of life? No, there couldn't.
21There can't have beenNo puede / pudo haber habido
There can't have been — SOLO frases negativas
✘ Negativa
There can't have been + sustantivo
There can't have been an evolution. (No pudo haber habido una evolución)
There can't have been an objective.
💬 Otras expresiones con There Be
22There have / has to beTiene que haber
There has to be → singular/incontable · There have to be → plural
✔ Afirmativa
There has to be a solution.
There have to be many good ideas to solve this.
✘ Negativa
There doesn't have to be a solution. (No tiene que haber…)
There don't have to be many good ideas.
? Pregunta
Does there have to be a solution?
Do there have to be many good ideas to solve this?
23There need(s) to beTiene que haber / Es necesario que haya
There needs to be → singular/incontable · There need to be → plural
✔ Afirmativa
There need to be rules.
There needs to be compensation for the accident.
✘ Negativa
There don't need to be rules.
There doesn't need to be compensation for the accident.
? Pregunta
Do there need to be rules?
Does there need to be compensation for the accident?
24There seem(s) to beParece haber
There seems to be → singular/incontable · There seem to be → plural
✔ Afirmativa
There seems to be a problem.
There seem to be fewer rich people.
✘ Negativa
There doesn't seem to be a problem.
There don't seem to be fewer rich people.
? Pregunta
Does there seem to be a problem?
Do there seem to be fewer rich people?
25There used to beSolía haber
Una sola forma: There used to be — en negativa y pregunta la «d» desaparece: use to
✔ Afirmativa
There used to be parks everywhere.
There used to be free food for the citizens.
✘ Negativa
There didn't use to be parks everywhere.
There didn't use to be free food for the citizens.
? Pregunta
Did there use to be parks everywhere?
Did there use to be free food for the citizens?
⚠️ Para no confundirte
THERE vs IT

THERE indica existencia (¿qué hay?); IT identifica o describe algo ya mencionado, el clima o la hora. There is a cat in the garden. It is black.

Some / Any

Afirmativa → SOME (There is some milk). Negativa y pregunta → ANY (There isn't any milk · Is there any milk?).

T10 — Question Words
1Las básicas

WHAT (qué), WHO (quién - sujeto/objeto), WHERE (dónde), WHEN (cuándo), WHY (por qué), HOW (cómo). What is your name? · Where do you live?

2WHICH vs WHAT

WHICH se usa cuando hay un número limitado y conocido de opciones (Which colour do you prefer, red or blue?); WHAT es más general/abierto (What colour is your car?).

3Combinaciones con HOW

How much (incontables/precio), How many (contables), How often (frecuencia), How long (duración), How far (distancia), How old (edad).

4WHOSE (posesión)

Pregunta de quién es algo: Whose book is this? (¿De quién es este libro?) — No confundir con WHO'S (who is / who has).

5WHO como sujeto vs objeto

Cuando WHO es el SUJETO de la pregunta, NO se usa el auxiliar DO/DID: Who called you? (no 'Who did call you'). Cuando es objeto, sí: Who(m) did you call?

6WHY + because

Las preguntas con WHY suelen responderse con BECAUSE: Why did you react that way? — Because I was tired.

7Subject questions negativas

Cuando WHO/WHAT es el sujeto pero la pregunta es negativa, SÍ se usa auxiliar: Who cried? (afirmativa, sin auxiliar) pero Who didn't cry? (negativa, con "did").

8Preguntas con preposición al final

Con verbos como speak with, talk about, belong to, agree with, la preposición se coloca al final de la pregunta: Who did you speak with? · Who does this car belong to?

9HOW ABOUT...? (sugerencias)

HOW ABOUT + sustantivo o verbo en gerundio para proponer algo: How about eating outside? · How about Japanese food?

10Exclamaciones con WHAT

WHAT + a/an + (adjetivo) + sustantivo contable singular: What a nice surprise! Sin "a/an", el sustantivo es plural o incontable: What stupid things you say! No hay inversión sujeto-verbo porque no es pregunta.

11Exclamaciones con HOW

HOW + adjetivo (How hard!) o HOW + adjetivo/adverbio + sujeto + verbo: How gracefully she dances! · How awesome this news is!

T11 — Question Tags
QUESTION TAG = coletilla al final de la frase, tras una coma («¿no?», «¿verdad?»). Se forma con verbo (auxiliar) + pronombre sujeto.
✔ frase afirmativa → ✘ tag negativo  ·  ✘ frase negativa → ✔ tag afirmativo
Mike and Peter are bored, aren't they? (nunca «aren't Mike and Peter?»: el sujeto pasa a pronombre)
My mum is happy, isn't she? · My mum isn't happy, is she?
🔹 Present Simple
1«To Be» (am / is / are)
Se repite el mismo verbo «be»
✔ Afirmativa
… am / is / are + not + sujeto
They are tall, aren't they? (Ellos son altos, ¿no?)
My mum is happy, isn't she?
✘ Negativa
… am / is / are + sujeto
We aren't in trouble, are we?
You aren't in the office, are you?
I am not nice, am I? (¡«Am I?» SÍ es correcto en negativa!)
2«Have got»
Solo existe en Present Simple. Se comporta como auxiliar
✔ Afirmativa
… have / has + not + sujeto
They have got a red car, haven't they?
He has got a daughter, hasn't he?
✘ Negativa
… have / has + sujeto
They haven't got a red car, have they?
He hasn't got a daughter, has he?
3«Have» (verbo normal)
«Have» NO es auxiliar aquí: necesita DO / DOES
✔ Afirmativa
… do / does + not + sujeto
They have a red car, don't they?
He has a daughter, doesn't he?
✘ Negativa
… do / does + sujeto
They don't have a red car, do they?
He doesn't have a daughter, does he?
4Verbos «normales» y semi-modales
Los que necesitan auxiliar para negar y preguntar (incluye semi-modales como need to): usan DO / DOES
✔ Afirmativa
… do / does + not + sujeto
We live in a nice house, don't we?
He eats pasta a lot, doesn't he?
She needs to leave soon, doesn't she? (semi-modal «need to»)
✘ Negativa
… do / does + sujeto
We don't live in a nice house, do we?
He doesn't eat pasta every day, does he?
She doesn't need to leave soon, does she?
5Verbos modales
Can, must, should, might… repiten el propio modal (un solo tiempo cada uno)
✔ Afirmativa
… modal + not + sujeto
You can do it, can't you?
They must be joking, mustn't they?
✘ Negativa
… modal + sujeto
We shouldn't call mum, should we?
It couldn't be worse, could it?
🔹 Pasado
6Past Simple «To Be» (was / were)
Se repite was / were
✔ Afirmativa
… was / were + not + sujeto
They were very rude, weren't they?
She was at the party, wasn't she?
✘ Negativa
… was / were + sujeto
They weren't very rude, were they?
She wasn't at the party, was she?
7Past Simple «normales»
Auxiliar DID
✔ Afirmativa
… did + not + sujeto
He had plenty of money, didn't he?
We ate a big burger, didn't we?
✘ Negativa
… did + sujeto
He didn't have plenty of money, did he?
We didn't eat a big burger, did we?
✨ A partir de aquí: todos los verbos se forman igual (con el auxiliar del tiempo)
8Present Continuous
Auxiliar: am / is / are
✔ Afirmativa
… am / is / are + not + sujeto
It is eating chicken, isn't it?
I am being silly, aren't I? (!!AREN'T I?!! (afirmativa))
✘ Negativa
… am / is / are + sujeto
It isn't eating chicken, is it?
I am not being silly, am I?
9Past Continuous
Auxiliar: was / were
✔ Afirmativa
… was / were + not + sujeto
You were late again, weren't you?
He was sad, wasn't he?
✘ Negativa
… was / were + sujeto
You weren't late again, were you?
He wasn't sad, was he?
10Present Perfect (Simple y Continuous)
Auxiliar: have / has
✔ Afirmativa
… have / has + not + sujeto
I have seen this movie, haven't I?
She has been driving all night, hasn't she?
✘ Negativa
… have / has + sujeto
I haven't seen this movie, have I?
They haven't been dating, have they?
11Past Perfect (Simple y Continuous)
Auxiliar: had
✔ Afirmativa
… had + not + sujeto
I had done it perfectly, hadn't I?
We had been dancing since 2 pm, hadn't we?
✘ Negativa
… had + sujeto
They hadn't called Mary before, had they?
She hadn't been writing her novel for a long time, had she?
🔮 Futuro y condicional
12Future con «will»
Will (también en Future Continuous, Perfect y Perfect Continuous)
✔ Afirmativa
… will + not + sujeto
I will win, won't I?
I will be flying then, won't I?
She will have finished at lunchtime, won't she?
✘ Negativa
… will + sujeto
They won't do it, will they?
The President won't be preparing his speech, will he?
Peter and I won't have arrived before her party, will we?
13«Be going to»
Funciona como «to be» (presente o pasado)
✔ Afirmativa
… am / is / are (was / were) + not + sujeto
He is going to visit his grandparents, isn't he?
They were going to catch him, weren't they?
✘ Negativa
… am / is / are (was / were) + sujeto
He isn't going to visit his grandparents, is he?
They weren't going to catch him, were they?
14Conditional (would)
Auxiliar: would
✔ Afirmativa
… would + not + sujeto
The party would be amazing, wouldn't it?
She would buy all of them, wouldn't she?
✘ Negativa
… would + sujeto
The party wouldn't be amazing, would it?
She wouldn't buy all of them, would she?
15Modales perfectos
Se repite el modal (must / should / ought to…)
✔ Afirmativa
… modal + not + sujeto
They must have arrived already, mustn't they?
She should have gone to the doctor, shouldn't she?
✘ Negativa
… modal + sujeto
They mustn't have called the police, must they?
She shouldn't have gone to the doctor, should she?
16Voz pasiva
El tag se hace con el «BE» (no con el participio)
✔ Afirmativa
… be (según tiempo) + not + sujeto
The homework is done by him, isn't it?
The car will be repaired by Susan, won't it?
✘ Negativa
… be (según tiempo) + sujeto
The essay hasn't been written by John, has it?
These papers hadn't been thrown away by the police, had they?
📣 Imperativos
17Let's / Let + pronombre / Imperativo
El tag es FIJO, sea la frase afirmativa o negativa
★ Ojo
«Let's» → SHALL WE
Let's go, shall we? (Vámonos, ¿vale?)
Let's not argue, shall we?
★ Ojo
«Let him / her / me / them» → WILL YOU
Let me help you, will you?
Don't let them do that to you, will you?
★ Ojo
Imperativo con infinitivo → WILL YOU
Shut up, will you?
Don't go there, will you?
⚠️ A tener en cuenta
Demostrativos

This / That → it: This is a mess, isn't it?
These / Those → they: These were prisoners, weren't they?

There Be

El pronombre del tag pasa a ser THERE: There is a house next to the hospital, isn't there? · There won't be journalists outside, will there?

Frases con significado negativo

Frase «afirmativa» con never, no, nobody, nothing, hardly, rarely… → el tag es AFIRMATIVO: You have never done this before, have you? · You have no money, have you? · Nobody called, did they?

T12 — Los Pronombres
Los pronombres sustituyen a sustantivos. Solo la 3ª persona del singular distingue género: he (masc.) · she (fem.) · it (cosas y animales).
1Subject PronounsPronombres sujeto
Hacen de sujeto: si aparecen, son quienes realizan la acción.
PronombreSignificaEjemplo
IYoI am Jack.
YouTúYou were at the party last night.
HeÉlHe works in a big company.
SheEllaShe has been living in London since 2000.
ItEllo / EsoIt is the biggest stadium ever built.
WeNosotros/asWe will go to the beach in summer.
YouVosotros/asYou should stop fighting.
TheyEllos/asThey were playing computer games.
2Object PronounsPronombres objeto
Reciben la acción: van después del verbo o de una preposición. She loves him (nunca «her loves he»).
PronombreSignificaEjemplo
Me(A) mí / meShe gave me the apple.
You(A) ti / teHe always calls you.
Him(A) él / le / loI don't understand him, he speaks too fast.
Her(A) ella / le / laWe received a letter from her yesterday.
It(A) ello / le / loMark can't find his watch, have you seen it?
Us(A) nosotros / nosThey won't be able to find us.
You(A) vosotros / osI can drive you to the airport.
Them(A) ellos / les / los / lasLeave them alone.
3Possessive AdjectivesAdjetivos posesivos
Van SIEMPRE + sustantivo. Its (sin apóstrofe) = posesivo; It's = it is / it has.
AdjetivoSignificaEjemplo
MyMiMy father is a journalist.
YourTuI like your car a lot.
HisSu (de él)He doesn't like his house.
HerSu (de ella)Her computer is better than mine.
ItsSu (cosa/animal)I like Japan and its culture.
OurNuestro/a/os/asOur children behave well.
YourVuestro/a/os/asHave you done your homework?
TheirSu (de ellos)Our neighbours are working in their garden.
4Possessive PronounsPronombres posesivos
Sustituyen al sustantivo: NO llevan sustantivo detrás. This is MY book (adjetivo) → This book is MINE (pronombre).
PronombreSignificaEjemplo
MineMío/a/os/asYou have your reasons, I have mine.
YoursTuyo/a/os/asIs this car yours? I love it!
HisSuyo (de él)This awful jacket is his.
HersSuyo (de ella)A friend of hers came to the house.
ItsSuyo (poco común)This toy is its.
OursNuestro/a/os/asThe money is ours.
YoursVuestro/a/os/asThe cake is yours.
TheirsSuyo (de ellos)My car is outside, theirs is in the garage.
5Reflexive PronounsPronombres reflexivos
Se usan cuando el objeto directo es el mismo que el sujeto (la acción recae en quien la hace): I hurt myself on the stairs. · Be careful, you can cut yourself. También para énfasis: I did it myself.
PronombreSignificaEjemplo
MyselfMe / yo mismoI blame myself for the fire.
YourselfTe / tú mismoYou should believe in yourself.
HimselfSe / él mismoTom hasn't been himself for days.
HerselfSe / ella mismaShe learned to read all by herself.
ItselfSe / a sí mismoThe cat threw itself in front of the car.
OurselvesNos / nosotros mismosWe can't finish by ourselves.
YourselvesOs / vosotros mismosThe decision has to be taken by yourselves.
ThemselvesSe / ellos mismosThey can make dinner by themselves.
6Verbos comunes con reflexivoTransitivos frecuentes
VerboSignificaEjemplo
BlameCulpar aI blame myself for the accident.
EnjoyDisfrutarWe really enjoyed ourselves on holiday.
HurtHacerse dañoBe careful, you can hurt yourself.
PreparePrepararDid they prepare everything themselves?
CutCortarShe cut herself with the knife.
HelpServir(se)Want something? Help yourselves.
IntroducePresentarLet me introduce myself.
KillMatarI was so embarrassed I wanted to kill myself.
⭐ Más puntos de examen
Indefinidos: SOME / ANY / NO + one / body / thing / where

SOME- en afirmativas y ofrecimientos (Would you like something?), ANY- en negativas y preguntas (Is there anybody here?), NO- ya es negativo por sí mismo (Nobody knows, sin otra negación).

EACH OTHER / ONE ANOTHER

Acción recíproca entre dos o más sujetos: They love each other (se aman mutuamente) — distinto de themselves (a sí mismos).

T13 — Sustantivos Contables e Incontables
1Contables

Se pueden contar y tienen plural: one apple, two apples. Admiten A/AN en singular y number + noun en plural.

2Incontables

No tienen plural y no llevan A/AN: water, rice, information, advice, furniture, money, news, luggage. Muchos de estos son plurales en español pero incontables en inglés (advice, information, furniture).

3Cuantificadores: MUCH/MANY/A LOT OF

MUCH + incontable (sobre todo negativas/preguntas: How much money?), MANY + contable plural (How many books?), A LOT OF/LOTS OF sirven para ambos, especialmente en afirmativas.

4FEW/A FEW vs LITTLE/A LITTLE

FEW/A FEW + contables plurales; LITTLE/A LITTLE + incontables. A FEW/A LITTLE = 'un poco, algo' (positivo); FEW/LITTLE (sin A) = 'casi nada, pocos' (negativo/escasez): I have a few friends (tengo algunos) vs I have few friends (tengo pocos, casi ninguno).

5Convertir incontable en contable

A PIECE OF / A BIT OF / A GLASS OF / A CUP OF + incontable: a piece of advice, a glass of water, a bit of information.

6Quantifiers: posición y A/AN

Quantifier + sustantivo (a bit of sugar) · + adjetivo + sustantivo (a few old books). A ante consonante, AN ante vocal; excepciones por el SONIDO: an hour, an honest man · a unit, a euro. Algunos pueden ser pronombres: I need some.

7Solo con CONTABLES plural

MANY (sobre todo negativas/preguntas), SO MANY, TOO MANY, A FEW (+) / FEW (−), SEVERAL, QUITE A FEW (bastantes), A COUPLE OF, BOTH, HUNDREDS / THOUSANDS / MILLIONS OF, A LARGE/SMALL NUMBER OF. Singular: EACH, EVERY, EITHER, NEITHER.

8Solo con INCONTABLES

MUCH, SO MUCH, TOO MUCH, A LITTLE (+) / LITTLE (−), A BIT OF, A GREAT/GOOD DEAL OF, A LARGE AMOUNT/QUANTITY OF. There is too much noise.

9SOME / ANY / NO / NONE

SOME: afirmativas y ofrecimientos/peticiones (Do you want some tea?), nunca negativas. ANY: negativas y preguntas; en afirmativa = "cualquiera" y NO con contable plural (any wine would do). NO + sustantivo (adjetivo) / NONE sustituye al sustantivo (pronombre); ambos solo en frases AFIRMATIVAS (ya son negativos): I have no money · He has two, I have none.

10Con contables e incontables

A LOT OF / LOTS OF / PLENTY OF, MOST, ENOUGH, ALL, MORE, SOME / ANY / NO / NONE. Ojo: A LOT / LOTS sin "of" son ADVERBIOS (I like you a lot), no quantifiers.

11Quantifier + OF

Sin "of" si hablamos en GENERAL (Most children like sweets). Con OF si va detrás the, posesivo, this/that/these/those, genitivo sajón u object pronoun: Most of the children · None of my friends · Few of these people · Both of us. Regla rápida: si hay "the" delante del sustantivo → SÍ "of".

12Cantidad y otros

HOW MUCH? incontables/precio · HOW MANY? contables plural. Sustantivos con doble sentido: light (luces C / luz I), stone (piedra C / material I), glass (vaso C / cristal I), wine (un vino C / el vino I). Estructura causativa: HAVE + objeto + participio → I had my car fixed (me lo arreglaron).

T14 — Presente Perfecto
1Forma

HAVE/HAS + participio pasado (verbo regular +ED, o 3ª columna de irregulares). I have worked · She has gone. Negativa: haven't/hasn't. Interrogativa: Have you...? / Has she...?

2Uso 1: experiencia vital (sin momento concreto)

I have been to Japan (en algún momento de mi vida, no importa cuándo). Se usa EVER en preguntas (Have you ever tried sushi?) y NEVER en negativas.

3Uso 2: acción pasada con resultado/relevancia en el presente

I have lost my keys (y ahora no las tengo, consecuencia presente) — distinto de Past Simple, que solo cuenta el hecho pasado sin conectarlo con ahora.

4Uso 3: acción que empezó en el pasado y continúa ahora

Con FOR (duración) y SINCE (punto de inicio): I have lived here for 10 years / since 2014.

5Uso 4: noticia reciente / acción recién terminada

Con JUST, ALREADY, YET: I have just finished · She has already left · Have you finished yet?

6Present Perfect vs Past Simple

Present Perfect: sin tiempo concreto o conectado al presente. Past Simple: tiempo concreto y terminado (I went to Japan in 2019, no 'I have gone... in 2019').

T15 — For, Since, Ago, Just, Still, Already, Yet
1FOR vs SINCE

FOR + duración/periodo de tiempo (for two years, for a long time). SINCE + punto de inicio concreto (since 2010, since Monday, since I was born). Ambos con Present Perfect.

2AGO

Indica 'hace X tiempo' desde AHORA, y se usa con Past Simple (nunca con Present Perfect): I finished two years ago (no 'I have finished two years ago').

3JUST

'Acabar de' — acción muy reciente, se coloca entre HAVE y el participio: I have just arrived.

4ALREADY

'Ya' — se usa en afirmativas para dar énfasis en que algo ha pasado antes de lo esperado; va entre HAVE y el participio, o al final: She has already left / She has left already.

5YET

'Todavía / ya' — se usa en negativas ('todavía no') y preguntas ('¿ya...?'), y va SIEMPRE al final de la frase: I haven't finished yet · Has she called yet?

6STILL

'Todavía' — indica que algo continúa (normalmente inesperado o que dura más de lo previsto); va ANTES del verbo principal (o después de BE/auxiliar): I still don't understand · She is still sleeping.

T16 — Present Perfect Continuo
1Forma

HAVE/HAS + BEEN + verbo-ING. I have been working · She has been studying. Pone el foco en la DURACIÓN o el proceso de la acción, no en el resultado.

2Uso: acción que empezó en el pasado y continúa (con foco en el proceso)

I have been waiting for an hour (llevo esperando, y sigo esperando o acabo de parar). Se usa con FOR/SINCE igual que Present Perfect simple.

3Uso: explicar una situación/resultado visible ahora

You're out of breath. Have you been running? — el resultado visible (sin aliento) se explica por el proceso reciente.

4Present Perfect Simple vs Continuo

Simple = foco en el resultado/cantidad terminada (I have read 3 books). Continuo = foco en el proceso/duración, sin importar si terminó (I have been reading all afternoon).

5Verbos de estado: no llevan forma continua

know, believe, understand, like, want, etc. no se usan en continuo (ni siquiera aquí): se usa Present Perfect simple: I have known her for years (no 'have been knowing').

T17 — Past Perfect
1Forma

HAD + participio pasado, igual para todas las personas. I had finished · She had finished. Negativa: hadn't. Interrogativa: Had you...?

2Uso: la acción más antigua de dos en el pasado

Cuando hay dos acciones pasadas, la que ocurrió PRIMERO va en Past Perfect y la más reciente en Past Simple: When I arrived, the film had already started (empezó antes de que yo llegara).

3Con BEFORE / AFTER / BY THE TIME

She had left before I arrived. · By the time we got there, they had gone. Ayudan a dejar claro el orden temporal, aunque a veces el orden ya se entiende sin Past Perfect.

4Reported Speech

El Past Perfect es el pasado del Present Perfect y del Past Simple al reportar lo que alguien dijo: 'I have finished' → She said she had finished.

5Trampa de examen

Si solo hay UNA acción pasada, o las acciones ocurren en el orden en que se cuentan, se usa Past Simple normal, NO Past Perfect: I woke up and had breakfast (orden lógico, sin necesidad de Past Perfect).

T18 — Past Perfect Continuo
1Forma

HAD + BEEN + verbo-ING. I had been working — igual para todas las personas.

2Uso: duración de una acción antes de otro momento pasado

I had been working for 3 hours when she called. Indica cuánto tiempo llevaba ocurriendo algo justo antes de que pasara otra cosa en el pasado.

3Uso: causa de un resultado pasado

He was tired because he had been running. El proceso previo explica la situación/resultado en el pasado (equivalente en pasado del Present Perfect Continuous).

4Past Perfect Simple vs Continuo

Simple: cantidad/resultado terminado (I had written 3 emails). Continuo: duración/proceso (I had been writing emails all morning).

T19 — Verbos Irregulares
1Qué son

Verbos cuyo pasado simple y/o participio pasado NO se forman con -ED, sino con una forma propia que debe memorizarse: go-went-gone, see-saw-seen, write-wrote-written.

2Los tres más usados como auxiliares/verbos especiales

BE: am/is/are - was/were - been. HAVE: have/has - had - had. DO: do/does - did - done.

3Grupos con patrón similar (ayuda a memorizar)

Terminados en -ING/-UNG: sing-sang-sung, ring-rang-rung, drink-drank-drunk. Terminados en -OUGHT: bring-brought-brought, buy-bought-bought, think-thought-thought, catch-caught-caught.

4Mismos en las 3 formas

cut-cut-cut, put-put-put, hit-hit-hit, cost-cost-cost, let-let-let, read-read-read (cambia la pronunciación, no la escritura).

5Muy frecuentes en el examen

go-went-gone, come-came-come, take-took-taken, give-gave-given, eat-ate-eaten, see-saw-seen, do-did-done, make-made-made, know-knew-known, break-broke-broken, choose-chose-chosen, speak-spoke-spoken.

T20 — Los Adverbios
1Formación

Adjetivo + LY: slow→slowly, careful→carefully. Consonante+Y → -ILY: happy→happily. Acabado en -LE: se quita la E y se añade Y: terrible→terribly. Acabado en -IC: +ALLY: basic→basically.

2Irregulares importantes

good→WELL (no 'goodly'), fast→fast, hard→hard, late→late, early→early. Estos últimos tienen la misma forma como adjetivo y como adverbio. HARDLY y LATELY existen pero cambian de significado (hardly = apenas; lately = últimamente).

3Posición: adverbios de frecuencia

Van antes del verbo principal, pero después de BE/auxiliares/modales: She often goes · She is often late · She has often gone.

4Posición: adverbios de modo

Normalmente van al final de la frase, después del verbo y el objeto: He drives carefully · She sings beautifully. Nunca entre el verbo y su objeto directo (no 'He opened carefully the door').

5Adverbios de grado (very, quite, too, enough)

VERY/QUITE van antes del adjetivo (very tired); TOO indica exceso negativo (too tired to walk); ENOUGH va DESPUÉS del adjetivo (tall enough, no 'enough tall').

6Tipos de adverbio y pregunta que responden

Modo How? (carefully) · Tiempo When? (tomorrow) · Duración How long? (all day) · Frecuencia How often? · Lugar Where? (there) · Grado To what degree? (really) · Orden (firstly, in the end) · Certeza How sure? (probably, definitely).

7Posición: reglas clave

Ante adjetivo/adverbio: extremely thin. Tras el verbo (y su objeto) los de modo/lugar/tiempo. Frecuencia: ante el verbo, tras BE y entre auxiliar y verbo (I had never been). Grado y certeza: ante el verbo, tras BE. NUNCA entre verbo y objeto. Con varios adverbios: MODO → LUGAR → TIEMPO. Para enfatizar: al inicio de la frase.

8Excepciones de formación

-E muda: true→truly (pero nicely, politely) · -Y→-ILY (happily) · consonante+-LE→-LY (sensibly) · -LL→+Y (fully) · -L→-LY (finally) · -IC→-ALLY (fantastically). Adjetivos que ACABAN en -ly (NO son adverbios): friendly, lively, lonely, lovely, silly → "in a friendly way/manner".

9Adverbios con dos formas (distinto significado)

high alto / highly muy · late tarde / lately últimamente · hard duro / hardly apenas · near cerca / nearly casi · most al máximo / mostly sobre todo · pretty bastante / prettily hermosamente · free gratis / freely libremente · right a la derecha / rightly con razón · wrong mal / wrongly erróneamente. Misma forma que el adjetivo: fast, early, daily, long, low, straight.

T21 — Comparativo y Superlativo
1Adjetivos cortos (1 sílaba)

+ER / +EST: tall→taller→the tallest. Si acaba en consonante-vocal-consonante, se dobla la consonante: big→bigger→the biggest. Si acaba en -E: solo +R/+ST: nice→nicer→the nicest.

2Adjetivos largos (2+ sílabas)

MORE / THE MOST + adjetivo: beautiful→more beautiful→the most beautiful. Excepción: adjetivos de 2 sílabas acabados en -Y cambian a -IER/-IEST: happy→happier→the happiest.

3Irregulares

good→better→the best, bad→worse→the worst, far→farther/further→the farthest/furthest, little→less→the least, many/much→more→the most.

4Comparaciones de igualdad e inferioridad

AS + adjetivo + AS (igualdad: as tall as), NOT AS/SO + adjetivo + AS (inferioridad: not as tall as), LESS + adjetivo + THAN (inferioridad formal: less expensive than).

5Comparativos dobles y progresivos

THE + comparativo, THE + comparativo (cuanto más... más...): The more you practise, the better you get. Repetición con AND para progresión: It's getting more and more difficult.

6Adjetivos con las dos formas y elder/eldest

clever, polite, simple, narrow, quiet admiten ambas: cleverer / more clever. ELDER / ELDEST solo en familia y SIEMPRE ante un sustantivo (my elder brother); ✗ He is the eldest · My brother is elder than me. OLDER vale para todo. Irregulares extra: well→better, few→fewer→the fewest (contable), little→less→the least (incontable), far→farther (físico) / further (figurado, "adicional").

7Inferioridad e igualdad

Inferioridad (todos igual, da igual la sílaba): NOT AS/SO + adj + AS · LESS + adj + THAN · superlativo THE LEAST + adj. Igualdad: AS + adj + AS (no hay superlativo de igualdad). Con cantidades: as much money as · as many people as.

8Adverbios: comparativo y superlativo

Una sílaba: fast→faster→the fastest. Dos o más sílabas, y TODOS los acabados en -ly: MORE / THE MOST (more seriously). Excepción: EARLY → earlier / the earliest. Irregulares: well→better→best, badly→worse→worst, far→further, much/many→more→most, little→less→least. Inferioridad: less easily · the least gracefully. Igualdad: as quickly as.

9THAN, ever y modificadores

THAN + object pronoun (taller than me), sustantivo (than Tom's cat) o subject pronoun + verbo (better than he did). Superlativo + present perfect con EVER: the tallest person I've ever seen. Intensifiers: much, far, a lot, quite, a great/good deal. Mitigators: a bit, a little bit, slightly, rather.

10LIKE vs AS

AS = en calidad de / rol (As your mother, I forbid it → soy tu madre; she works as a secretary); también as you know, as expected, as I said, as requested, such as; comparativo de igualdad (as well as me). LIKE = parecido a (Like your mother, I forbid it → opino igual que ella); look like = parecerse; ejemplos (sports like football). LIKE no sirve para la igualdad "as…as".

T22 — Las Preposiciones
1Tiempo: AT / ON / IN

AT: horas y momentos puntuales (at 5pm, at night, at Christmas). ON: días y fechas (on Monday, on 3rd May). IN: periodos largos (in July, in 2020, in the morning, in winter).

2Lugar: AT / ON / IN

AT: punto concreto (at the bus stop, at home). ON: superficie (on the table, on the wall). IN: espacio cerrado/delimitado (in the box, in London, in bed).

3Movimiento: TO / INTO / FROM

TO indica dirección/destino (go to school), INTO indica entrar en un espacio (walk into the room), FROM indica origen (I'm from Spain).

4Preposiciones tras adjetivos y verbos comunes

good AT, afraid OF, interested IN, married TO, similar TO, depend ON, listen TO, look AT/FOR, wait FOR, arrive AT/IN (at + lugar pequeño, in + ciudad/país).

5BY vs UNTIL

BY = como fecha límite, una sola vez, antes de o en ese momento (Finish it by Friday). UNTIL = duración continuada hasta ese momento (I'll wait until Friday).

6IN (lugar): más usos

Área/espacio cerrado y ciudades/países; puntos cardinales; habitaciones; agua (in the river/pool); in hospital (ingresado) · in prison (preso) · in the sky · in the middle · in a photo/picture · in a queue/line/row.

7AT (lugar) y ON (lugar)

AT: edificio como punto de encuentro o por su función (at the theatre), lugares comunes (at home/work/school), puntos concretos (at the door, at the traffic lights), posición (at the top/bottom/end). She was at the hospital = trabajaba/acompañaba; ingresado = in hospital. ON: superficie y pisos (on the 5th floor), partes del cuerpo, on the radio/TV, on the left/right, transportes cuando vas subido (on the bus; by bus = el medio; on foot).

8Tiempo: AT / ON / IN — lista rápida

AT: horas, Christmas/Easter, night, the weekend, the moment, present, the same time, lunchtime, midnight/midday, last. ON: días, fechas, días con "day" (Christmas Day, my birthday, New Year's Eve), on holidays, on Saturday morning. IN: meses, años, estaciones, décadas/siglos, partes del día (in the morning/afternoon/evening, pero at night) y plazo futuro (in two weeks).

9Verbo + preposición (muy frecuentes)

accuse sb OF sth · blame sb FOR sth · listen TO · look AT · remind sb OF sth (algo externo te lo recuerda) / remind sb OF sb (te recuerda a alguien) / remind sb ABOUT sth (recordar una tarea) · thank sb FOR · wait FOR · write TO · worry ABOUT · speak TO/WITH. Solo se pone la preposición si hay objeto: She is always speaking / She doesn't speak to me.

10Adjetivo + preposición y sustantivo + preposición

afraid OF · angry ABOUT (situación) / angry WITH (persona) · jealous OF · proud OF · ready FOR. Detrás: object pronoun, reflexivo si es la misma persona (angry with myself) y verbo en -ING (accused of stealing). Sustantivos: answer/solution TO · interest IN · knowledge OF · reason FOR · connection WITH · sympathy FOR (misma preposición que el verbo del que vienen).

11Preposición al FINAL (preguntas y relativas)

En preguntas (también indirectas) la preposición va al final: Who are you looking at? · What are you good at? · I don't know who she lives with. En subordinadas y relativas igual: That's the exam (that) I'm preparing for · You don't know what I'm capable of.

T23 — Despite, In Spite Of, Although, Though, Even Though
Todos expresan CONTRASTE entre dos ideas. Se dividen en dos grupos según lo que va detrás.
① DESPITE / IN SPITE OF + sustantivo · -ing · the fact that
② ALTHOUGH / EVEN THOUGH / THOUGH + oración (sujeto + verbo)
1Despite / In spite of«A pesar de»
Detrás de Despite / In spite of: sustantivo, -ing o the fact that + oración.
✔ Afirmativa
Formas CORRECTAS: se usan EXACTAMENTE igual. No mezcles sus partículas.
Despite · In spite of
✘ Negativa
Formas INCORRECTAS
Despite of · In spite · In despite · Spite
✔ Afirmativa
+ sustantivo / pronombre
Despite the rain, we went camping. (A pesar de la lluvia…)
I understood everything in spite of his accent.
✔ Afirmativa
+ verbo en -ING
In spite of being young, he had a great job.
Despite not being 18, he tried to enter the disco. (Negativo: NOT delante del -ing)
✔ Afirmativa
+ THE FACT THAT + oración
Despite the fact that I was very tired, I enjoyed the movie.
My mum was happy in spite of the fact that the present wasn't what she wanted.
✘ Negativa
Sin «the fact that» NUNCA va una frase detrás
Despite I was tired, I enjoyed the movie.
In spite of have a car, I went on foot.
2Although / Even though / Though«Aunque»
Detrás de Although / Even though / Though va siempre una oración completa.
Los tres significan «aunque» y se usan igual; solo cambia la formalidad:
Even though → FORMAL / enfático (escritura)Although → NEUTROThough → INFORMAL (hablado)
✔ Afirmativa
+ oración (sujeto + verbo)
Although I was angry, he made me laugh. (Aunque estaba enfadada…)
Even though it was raining, we went outside.
Though it was dark, they went for a walk and got lost.
✘ Negativa
NUNCA + sustantivo ni -ing
Although having a headache, I went out.
Even though the rain, I went out.
★ Ojo
«Though» al final de la frase, tras coma = «pero / sin embargo»
Maths is difficult; it's interesting, though. (…pero son interesantes)
⚠️ Trampas de examen
Despite of NO EXISTE

Se dice DESPITE (solo) o IN SPITE OF (con OF). Y nunca «Despite it was raining» (eso pide ALTHOUGH).

Regla rápida

¿Detrás hay sujeto + verbo? → ALTHOUGH. ¿Hay sustantivo o -ing? → DESPITE / IN SPITE OF.

T24 — Conectores
1Adición

AND, ALSO, MOREOVER, IN ADDITION, FURTHERMORE, BESIDES. She is smart. Moreover, she is very hard-working.

2Contraste

BUT, HOWEVER, ON THE OTHER HAND, WHEREAS, WHILE. HOWEVER suele ir al principio de frase con coma: He is rich. However, he is not happy.

3Causa y efecto

BECAUSE/BECAUSE OF (+ sustantivo), SINCE, AS (causa), SO, THEREFORE, AS A RESULT, CONSEQUENTLY. It was raining, so we stayed home. · She was late because of the traffic.

4Finalidad

SO THAT + sujeto+verbo (para que), IN ORDER TO + infinitivo (para). I study hard so that I can pass. · I study hard in order to pass.

5Secuencia

FIRST(LY), THEN, NEXT, AFTER THAT, FINALLY. Organizan ideas en orden cronológico o de importancia.

6Ejemplos

FOR EXAMPLE / FOR INSTANCE (con coma y frase completa) · SUCH AS (tras coma + sustantivos o -ING): I have hobbies, such as painting and running.

7ALSO: posición

Ante el verbo principal, pero DETRÁS de BE (I am also a writer · I can also drive); a veces al inicio con coma: Also, I need to…

8Contraste: más conectores

HOWEVER / NEVERTHELESS / NONETHELESS (sin embargo, con coma y frase) · ON THE ONE HAND… ON THE OTHER HAND (por un lado… por otro, con coma + sujeto + verbo).

T25 — Futuro Simple y Futuro Perfecto
1WILL (futuro simple)

Sujeto + WILL + verbo base, igual para todas las personas: I will help you. Se usa para decisiones espontáneas (en el momento de hablar), predicciones sin pruebas/opiniones, promesas y ofrecimientos: I think it will rain · I'll carry that for you.

2GOING TO (futuro con intención/evidencia)

BE + GOING TO + verbo base: para planes/intenciones ya decididas (I'm going to study medicine) y predicciones CON pruebas visibles ahora (Look at those clouds, it's going to rain).

3Futuro Perfecto: forma y uso

WILL HAVE + participio pasado: By 2030, I will have finished my degree. Expresa una acción que estará COMPLETADA antes de un momento futuro concreto (con BY + fecha/momento).

4WILL vs GOING TO: la clave

WILL = decisión en el momento / opinión sin pruebas. GOING TO = plan ya decidido antes / evidencia visible ahora de que algo va a pasar.

T26 — Futuro Continuo y Perfecto Continuo
1Futuro Continuo: forma

WILL BE + verbo-ING. This time tomorrow, I will be flying to New York.

2Futuro Continuo: uso
